surface_mechanism_description: Exposure of the substrate to TMG results in rapid deposition of adsorbate complexes that block active surface sites. Further adsorption occurs only when blocked sites are exposed by desorption or decomposition of initial adsorbates. The reaction leading to the production of atomic H in the gas phase is particularly relevant to the alternating-exposure growth technique. Adsorbed CH3 that desorbs from the substrate surface can react with H2, producing CH4 and atomic H in the boundary layer. The atomic H then reacts with the CH3Ga adsorbate to produce Ga on the surface and CH4 in the gas phase.
evidence: According to the steric hindrance model for low-temperature growth of GaAs by the alternating-exposure technique, exposure of the substrate to TMG results in rapid deposition, on the active surface sites, of adsorbate complexes that are large enough to block a number of adjacent sites. After all the active sites are either occupied or blocked, further adsorption can occur only as the blocked sites are exposed by desorption or decomposition of the initial adsorbates. When the TMG injection time is insufficient, the number of active sites is limited, and therefore the number of Ga atoms deposited per TMG cycle will be less than a monolayer as observed in our experiments. We speculate that adsorbed CH3 that desorbs from the substrate surface can react with H2, which produces CH4 and atomic H in the boundary layer. The atomic H then reacts with the CH3Ga adsorbate to produce Ga on the surface and CH4 in the gas phase.
